vulnerabilities.title: PREDICTABLE_TARGET_DERIVATION_FROM_USER_INPUT

root_cause.description: The game's target number is not randomly generated. Instead, it is derived from the player's own guess input: target = (guess % 10) + 1, computed via imul 0x66666667 magic division at 0x1855-0x1882, stored at [rbp-0x3c], then compared against the guess itself at 0x188b (cmp edx, eax). For any guess value in the range 1..10, (guess % 10) + 1 equals guess, so the comparison guess == target always succeeds. The attacker controls both sides of the equality check, making every round a guaranteed win. This allows the player to accumulate money via money += bet (at 0x18a6) until exceeding the 1,000,000 win threshold (cmp rax, 0xf4240 at 0x18cc), causing game3 to return and main to call print_flag.

data_flow: if equal: money = money + bet at 0x18a6
main calls print_flag after game3 returns

security_check.expected: The target number should be randomly generated (e.g., via rand()/random()) and independent of the player's guess input, so the player cannot predict or control it.
security_check.actual: The target is computed as (guess % 10) + 1 from the player's own guess input, then compared to that same guess. No randomness is involved.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing random number generation. The target derivation function f(x) = (x % 10) + 1 has fixed points at x = 1..10 where f(x) = x, making the comparison trivially satisfiable.

vulnerable_operation.operation: Comparison of user input against a value derived from that same input

impact.reason: The game's win condition (money > 1,000,000) is reachable by any player who guesses a value in 1..10, since the target always equals the guess. This bypasses the intended game logic where winning should be probabilistic. Reaching the win condition causes game3 to return, and main then calls print_flag which reads and prints /flag.txt. The attacker can set bet=500 (initial money) and guess any value 1-10 repeatedly to accumulate money past the threshold.

evidence.description: Target computation: mov ecx,[rbp-0x40]; movsxd rax,ecx; imul rax,rax,0x66666667; shr rax,0x20; sar eax,0x2; ... sub ecx,eax; lea eax,[rdx+0x1]; mov [rbp-0x3c],eax. This computes (guess % 10) + 1 from the guess input.
cmp edx,eax compares [rbp-0x40] (guess) with [rbp-0x3c] (target=(guess%10)+1). For guess in 1..10, target==guess, so jne at 0x188d is not taken, entering the win path.

On win path: money += bet (add rax,rdx at 0x18a6); then cmp rax,0xf4240; jle 0x18f4 (continue loop); jmp 0x1977 (return). Since every guess wins, player accumulates money until > 1,000,000, then game3 returns to main which calls print_flag.
call game3; call print_flag — print_flag is called unconditionally after game3 returns, reading /flag.txt and printing it.

verification_required: Dynamic verification: run the binary, input Y, bet 500, guess 5 repeatedly, confirm money accumulates and flag is printed

vulnerabilities.title: STACK_BUFFER_OVERFLOW_VIA_UNBOUNDED_Scanf_S

root_cause.description: scanf("%s", [rbp-0x60]) at 0x172c (first round) and 0x191e (continue round) writes to the ready_choice stack buffer at [rbp-0x60] with no width limit. The format string at 0x2280 is bare "%s" (confirmed in .rodata). The strlen-based bounds check is applied AFTER the write has already occurred (at 0x174c for first round, 0x193e for continue round). The buffer at [rbp-0x60] is only 16 bytes before the money variable at [rbp-0x50], 24 bytes before bet at [rbp-0x48], 32 bytes before guess at [rbp-0x40], and 88 bytes before the stack canary at [rbp-0x08]. In the continue round, the post-write strlen check allows up to 100 bytes (cmp rax, 0x64; ja at 0x1942), which exceeds the 88-byte distance to the canary. Input between 17 and 88 bytes overwrites the game state variables (money, bet, guess, target) without triggering the canary, since the canary is at offset 88 from the buffer start.

data_flow: stdin -> scanf("%s", [rbp-0x60]) at 0x191e (continue round) — unbounded write
bytes 40-87: overwrite stack strings and padding
strlen check at 0x193e occurs AFTER the write — too late to prevent corruption

security_check.expected: Input length should be bounded BEFORE writing to the buffer, e.g., using scanf("%15s", buf) or fgets(buf, size, stdin).
security_check.actual: scanf("%s") writes unbounded data first, then strlen is checked post-write. First round allows <=15 bytes (just fits before money at offset 16, but null terminator lands on money LSB). Continue round allows <=100 bytes, which exceeds the 88-byte distance to the canary.
security_check.missing_or_incorrect: Missing width specifier in scanf format string. Post-write length check cannot prevent the overflow that has already occurred. The continue round threshold (100) is larger than the buffer-to-canary distance (88), allowing canary corruption.

vulnerable_operation.target: [rbp-0x60] ready_choice buffer and adjacent stack variables (money, bet, guess, target, canary)
vulnerable_operation.size: unbounded (limited only by input length; post-write check allows up to 100 bytes in continue round)

impact.reason: In the continue round, input of 17-87 bytes overwrites the money variable at [rbp-0x50] (offset 16 from buffer) without triggering the stack canary (at offset 88). This allows the attacker to set money to an arbitrary value, potentially bypassing the win condition (money > 1,000,000) directly. The bet and guess variables can also be overwritten. The post-write strlen check (<=100) passes for inputs under 100 bytes, and the Y/N check only examines the first byte.

Input of 88+ bytes in the continue round overwrites the stack canary at [rbp-0x08], which is detected by __stack_chk_fail at function return. Input between 88 and 100 bytes corrupts the canary and potentially the saved rbp/return address, but the canary check at 0x197c-0x198b aborts the process before return. The overflow itself is a memory corruption of the stack frame.
Input of 88+ bytes corrupts the stack canary, causing __stack_chk_fail to be called at 0x198b, terminating the process with a stack smashing detected error.

evidence.description: Format string at 0x2280 in .rodata is bare "%s" (confirmed via hex dump: 25 73 00), with no width specifier. Used by scanf at 0x172c (first round) and 0x191e (continue round).
Continue round: call scanf at 0x191e writes to [rbp-0x60], then strlen is called at 0x1939, then cmp rax,0x64 at 0x193e checks <=100. The write occurs BEFORE the check.

After the strlen check passes (<=100), only the first byte of [rbp-0x60] is checked for 'Y' (0x59) or 'y' (0x79) at 0x1944/0x1954. If the first byte is Y/y, execution jumps to 0x1798 (bet prompt) with corrupted money/bet/guess values still in place. The overwritten money at [rbp-0x50] is used directly in the bet comparison and win check.

Stack layout: [rbp-0x60] buffer, [rbp-0x50] money (0x1f4=500), [rbp-0x48] bet (0x1f4=500), [rbp-0x40] guess, [rbp-0x3c] target, [rbp-0x08] canary. Distance from buffer to money = 0x60-0x50 = 16 bytes; to canary = 0x60-0x08 = 88 bytes.

Verify whether overwritten money value persists through the bet prompt loop and triggers the win condition
Verify canary detection behavior for inputs >= 88 bytes

vulnerabilities.title: SIGNED_INTEGER_OVERFLOW_IN_MONEY_PLUS_BET

root_cause.description: The money update operation at 0x18a6 performs money = money + bet (add rax, rdx) using signed 64-bit arithmetic. The bet variable at [rbp-0x48] is read via scanf(%lld) as a signed 64-bit integer. The bet validation only checks bet >= 0 (jns at 0x17d2) and money - bet >= 0 (jns at 0x17fd). There is no check that money + bet does not overflow INT64_MAX (0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF). If money + bet overflows, the result wraps to a negative value. However, the win check at 0x18cc uses 'cmp rax, 0xf4240; jle' (signed comparison), so a wrapped negative value would not satisfy money > 1000000. Conversely, if money is already large and bet is chosen to make money+bet wrap to a value > 1000000 but still positive, the win condition could be triggered via overflow rather than legitimate accumulation. This is a secondary path to the win condition, independent of the target derivation flaw (BUG-001).

money - bet >= 0 check (jns at 0x17fd) — signed subtraction, may wrap
money = money + bet (add rax, rdx at 0x18a6) — signed 64-bit add, may overflow
cmp money, 0xf4240; jle (signed comparison at 0x18cc) — win if money > 1000000

security_check.actual: Only bet >= 0 and money - bet >= 0 are checked. No overflow check on money + bet. The bet can be any non-negative int64 value, and money - bet uses signed subtraction which can wrap if bet > money (but this is caught by jns). However, the money + bet addition at 0x18a6 has no overflow protection.

impact.reason: If money + bet overflows INT64_MAX, the money variable wraps to a negative or unexpected positive value. This could potentially set money to a value > 1,000,000 via overflow rather than legitimate accumulation, bypassing the intended game progression. However, this requires money to already be very large (close to INT64_MAX), which itself requires many winning rounds — achievable via BUG-001. The overflow path is a secondary concern.

evidence.description: add rax, rdx performs money = money + bet with no overflow check. rax=[rbp-0x50] (money), rdx=[rbp-0x48] (bet). Both are signed 64-bit.
